title: Ordinary evaluation of the adjunction-normalized pullback compositor
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E/Q_ell and composable scheme maps h: Z -> X and f: X -> Y. For every index n>=0 and every strict coefficient system M on Y, evaluate the canonical ordinary whole-system pullback compositor at n. Under the unit-normalized ordinary evaluation isomorphisms of lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison, the result equals the canonical finite coefficient module compositor of lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition. Explicitly, e_(hf)^(-1) followed by ev_n(a_M) equals a_(M_n) followed by h_n^*(e_f^(-1)) followed by e_h^(-1). Here n denotes the positive quotient exponent n+1. No normalization hypothesis on M or replacement of its transitions is assumed.

proof.text: Obtain the direct-image mates d and delta of the system and finite compositors from their existing unique-existence statements. Retain the stated section formulas and conjugateIsoEquiv equalities. The unit normalization of inverseEvaluation supplies the ordinary evaluation unit equation for each of f, h and h composed with f.

The proved direct-evaluation section API identifies every component of its eqToIso comparison with the identity on sections, by equality elimination and congr_heq. Thus evaluating d and then comparing direct images agrees with comparing the two direct images and applying delta: both section formulas restrict along the same fibre-product-pasting isomorphism. This holds for every system, without conditions on its transitions.

Prove the abstract evaluated-transpose identity from homEquiv_unit, naturality of the direct evaluation square and its unit normalization. Prove that horizontal composition of two such squares satisfies the composite unit equation using comp_unit_app and naturality. Transpose the evaluated system compositor through the finite adjunction, use unit_conjugateEquiv for the two compositor mates, the direct-image square equality of the preceding step, and the composite unit equation. Injectivity of homEquiv gives equality after the forward evaluation comparisons. Cancel these isomorphisms to obtain exactly the displayed inverse-evaluation formula.

theorem ordinaryCompositionEvaluation {X Y Z : Scheme.{t}}
    (h : Z ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ) (M : coefficientSequenceModules l E Y) :
    (ordinaryEvaluation l E (h ≫ f) n).inv.app M ≫
      (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Z n).map
        ((integralComparisonSequenceComposition l E h f).hom.app M) =
    (Scheme.coefficientModulePullbackComposition h f
      (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{t + 1}
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))))).hom.app
          ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n).obj M) ≫
      (integralOperationsLevelPullback l E h n).map
        ((ordinaryEvaluation l E f n).inv.app M) ≫
      (ordinaryEvaluation l E h n).inv.app
        ((integralComparisonSequencePullback l E f).obj M)
